evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (0.04 s) and diffed with experiments/results.txt: identical. Recomputed independently without importing the subject, from the Schervish (1989) / Buja-Stuetzle-Shen (2005) weight-function representation of binary proper scores, l(r,1)=int_r^1 (1-q)w(q)dq, l(r,0)=int_0^r q w(q)dq with w=G'' (1/(q(1-q)) inside, c=1/(eps(1-eps)) outside), by Simpson quadrature (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/a3a7f90a-8376-570c-8a4f-69ce15ac73b5/scratchpad/tangent/indep.py). It reproduces R_eps for all six eps in E1 to 4 decimals (2.6363 ... 14.8155), kappa -0.098144/-0.024978/-0.000500, the E2 efficiencies 126.58/126.58/12.77/1.41/0.51 and ratio 63.29, the four crossovers 0.2544/0.1466/0.099/0.0678 (by bisection on w(p)/R=2, not the closed form), the E3 expected losses 0.0079/0.0093/0.0102/0.0102/0.0102, and the E4 p=0.001 values 126.585/111.144/49.101. Defects: no validation that 0<eps<1/2 (efficiency(0.3, 0.9) silently returns 1.424, and run.py:23 prints it); `from tangent_log import *` in tests and run.py; test_model.py:36 uses `assert... if p > eps else None` as a statement; run.py is an unstructured script. Acceptable for a research note: 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: every number in README:3 and the paper's sections 1-4 matches results.txt and my recomputation; the abstract honestly says 'an application of standard Bregman/proper-scoring facts ... not a new theory'; limits (binary, risk-neutral, multiclass untested) are stated. Not backed: whitepaper.md:18 'the excess saturates at ~pR_eps' is the saturated expected loss, not the excess (excess at r=0 is 0.00235 vs pR=0.0102, from the subject's own exp_loss); the same paragraph says r=1e-9 'loses 0.0207 ... vs 0.0102', quoting total expected loss, of which 0.0079 is paid by the truthful report too (misreport cost 0.0128 vs 0.0023). README:3 'worse than Brier for p above a closed-form crossover' holds only on [crossover, 1-crossover] (symmetric score). The '63x Brier' headline is a comparison inside the tangent family at a cutoff tuned to the truth, which neither README nor paper says; over all bounded proper scores curvature per range is unbounded (a weight box on [p/2,3p/2] gives 1001 at p=1e-3, {S}/baseline.py). whitepaper.md:6 names Savage, Gneiting-Raftery, Frongillo-Waggoner with no reference list. 2.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on the construction: it is correct, closed-form and tested. Nearest prior work: the Schervish (1989) / Buja, Stuetzle and Shen (2005) representation, in which every binary proper score is a weight function w=G'' and this construction is just w(q)=1/(q(1-q)) clipped to a constant outside [eps,1-eps]; tailored and Beta-family scores (Johnstone, Jose and Winkler 2011; Merkle and Steyvers 2013); and optimisation of scoring rules under a bounded payment range for incentive strength (Neyman, Noarov and Weinberg, EC 2021, 'Binary scoring rules that incentivize precision'; Li, Hartline, Shan and Wu, EC 2022, 'Optimization of scoring rules'). None is cited. The result is sound but not new, and the paper says so. Missing baselines: Brier is the only comparator; I ran the Beta family w=q^(a-1)(1-q)^(b-1) (a in 0.01..1, b in 0.05..4) and its best efficiency at p=1e-3 is 74.05 at (0.2, 4.0), below tangent-log's 126.58 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/a3a7f90a-8376-570c-8a4f-69ce15ac73b5/scratchpad/tangent/baseline.py), a favourable comparison the paper could have made. The 'eps=p is best' result needs the truth p, which is what is being elicited; there is no analysis over a prior or a range of p. No model of stake, slashing or verifier effort despite the application framing. 2.
evidence.domain: Against standard proper-scoring practice (Gneiting and Raftery 2007; Schervish 1989): the construction and its strict propriety, range and log-equivalence are correct and would pass. Departures an EC reviewer would hit: (1) the objective 'curvature at the truth per unit of range' is a local, known-truth measure; incentive-for-precision work optimises expected score gain from information over the range bound, where the optimum is a V-shaped/threshold score, not a log variant; (2) the optimality claims (63x, eps=p) are within the one-parameter family and at a known p; (3) the saturation claim about deterrence is misstated by 4.3x; (4) no reference list. 2.

verdict: A small, correct note. Every number in results.txt reproduces exactly on rerun and matches an independent quadrature of the Schervish/Buja weight-function representation (R_eps for six eps, kappa, the 126.58 efficiency and 63x ratio, four crossovers by bisection, the E3 misreport losses). The tests are real: 7 of 8 seeded mutations were caught, and only the unguarded eps domain slipped through. It misses the bar on claims: the paper's statement that the misreport excess saturates at pR_eps is wrong by 4.3x, the 63x and eps=p results are within-family, known-truth comparisons against Brier only, and the paper has no reference list although it re-derives a clipped Schervish weight function that an EC reviewer would recognise at once. Finished as scoped (completeness 3). Fitness and domain are 2: sound, but not new, and not yet placed against the bounded-range scoring-rule literature.
